"Cough, cough... kid, care for a bun?" The old man gazed at the moon in the night sky. 
Relying on alms, the old man pulled Celestial Candle all the way west. They had no destination, just walked. 
At first, Celestial Candle was afraid of water, so the old man pushed her. Slowly, the girl dared to walk ahead, testing the river's depth with her feet. 
The two supported each other through pass after pass. Only, the old man's back grew more hunched, while Celestial Candle remained silent. 
"You're afraid to eat the bun because, back when your parents sold you..." The old man paused. 
"On this journey, though we aren't close, I know you're a good kid." 
"Kid, don't be afraid of anything, and don't go hungry." 
"My journey ends here. From now on, when you're hungry or tired, look for food in the water." 
"But test the depth before you go in." 
"They say the moon in the water can turn into a bun. I wonder what it tastes like..." 
"How does that song go again... 'Moonlight bright, cast your net right... eat a bun, little one...'" 
The old man's voice faded, finally dissolving into the water like moonlight. 
After a long while, the sound of the girl's weeping came, like a rain that never ceased years ago.

5648156706522609309: By decree of the Ghostlight Market, all merchants must leave by the fourth watch. None may linger until dawn. Yet one wine peddler, drunk as usual, passes out in the street and fails to leave in time. As he drifts between sleep and waking, a distant Gong suddenly rings out. Fog sweeps across the sky, and wraiths wander silently through the mist. Terrified, he flees in a daze, glimpsing flashes of past glory and perhaps the land of the dead. In his panic, he stumbles into the waters of Huang Quan. Flailing helplessly, he grasps the bulb of a red spider lily growing by the riverbank. Moments later, an icy chill spreads through his body. His senses return, and the illusions vanish. When the fog clears and he awakes, he understands its mystery: wine brewed from the flower's stamen causes hallucinations; wine brewed from its bulb chills the heart and wipes away memories. Thus, the second drink, Oblivion Crossing, is born.
